known_limitations: Synthetic operators built in a real Schur basis with strictly block-upper non-normal perturbations; this is a controlled construction, not a biologically sampled sparse synaptic matrix, and realistic sparsity-induced non-normality may behave differently. The Kreiss constant is approximated on a finite grid of z outside the unit circle (24 radii x 72 angles); the reported value is a lower bound on the true supremum, sufficient for the rank-ordering and regression used here. Transient amplification sup_t||A^t|| is computed over a finite horizon (t=1..400 in Experiment A, 300 in B); for spectral radius < 1 the peak is captured well before decay. Memory capacity is measured in a simplified noisy linear reservoir (single fixed input vector, Ridge readout, noise 1e-2); input direction, readout structure and nonlinearity can change the picture, and the memory result is contested in the duel and is NOT a clean confirmation of the thesis. Experiment C uses one specific chain construction; it shows memory differs at identical spectrum but does not establish that non-normality monotonically governs memory.
